evals.prompt: Can you review the Go service in evals/go-quality-review/fixtures/orders-api? We're about to put it into production next week and I want to know how solid it is and what to fix first.
evals.expected_output: Low grade (D/F or capped at C at most). Critical findings: data race on global Orders map, goroutine leak in fetch.FetchAll on early return, unclosed resp.Body, http.Get without timeout, math/rand tokens, ignored Decode/Encode errors. Major: log-and-return, string-compare errors, log.Fatal in library, utils package, mutable global state.
expectations: Identifies the data race on the package-level Orders map written from concurrent HTTP handlers
Identifies the goroutine leak in fetch.FetchAll when it returns early on the first error (unbuffered channel)
Flags that resp.Body is never closed in fetch.FetchAll
Flags HTTP calls/server without timeouts (http.Get default client or ListenAndServe without timeouts)
Flags math/rand used to generate order IDs/tokens
Flags ignored errors from json Decode or Encode
Flags error both logged and returned (store.Save or handler)
Flags comparing errors by err.Error() string instead of errors.Is
Gives an explicit verdict that the service is not production-ready (low grade or equivalent)
Findings cite file:line locations
Flags SSRF: /prices fetches URLs supplied by the client
Marks at least one critical concurrency finding (race or goroutine leak) as confirmed by running code

evals.prompt: I wrote a small rate limiter library at evals/go-quality-review/fixtures/ratelimit and plan to open-source it. How's the code quality? Give me an honest grade.
evals.expected_output: High grade (A or B). No critical findings. Few minor findings at most; credits table-driven tests, context use, mutex discipline, docs.
expectations: Gives a high overall verdict (grade A or B, or equivalent strongly positive assessment)
Reports no critical or high-severity defects
Does not falsely claim a data race or goroutine leak in the library
Explicitly credits specific strengths (e.g. table-driven tests, context cancellation, mutex discipline, doc comments)
Findings, if any, cite file:line locations
Flags that a rate of 0 (or invalid arguments) makes the wait-time calculation divide by zero

evals.prompt: audit the go code in evals/go-quality-review/fixtures/logsum - it's a little log summarizing CLI I hacked together. what should I clean up?
evals.expected_output: Mid grade (B/C). No critical findings. Flags: gofmt on main.go, stutter ParserConfig, RequestId initialism, missing doc comments, else after return, %v instead of %w, boolean flag params, copy-paste tests without table, logic in main.
expectations: Flags that main.go is not gofmt-formatted
Flags %v used instead of %w when wrapping the time.Parse error
Flags the boolean flag parameters of ParseAll (skipBad, debugOnly)
Flags copy-pasted tests that should be table-driven
Flags naming issues: ParserConfig stutter or RequestId initialism
Flags summarization logic living in main and being untestable
Reports no critical-severity findings and gives a mid-range verdict (not A, not F)
Findings cite file:line locations
Flags the nondeterministic top-5 ordering when error counts tie
